Photograph: Royal Navy/AFP/Getty Images Russia-Ukraine war at a glance Ukraine Explainer Ukraine war briefing: Nato ‘foils Russian undersea cable sabotage drill’ Swindon drone factory was target of Russia plot involving British man, court hears; Poland says Ukraine border crossing came under threat. What we know on day 1,661 Warren Murray and agencies Thu 10 Sep 2026 22.31 EDT Last modified on Fri 11 Sep 2026 01.29 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Nato forces chased away Russian ships in Arctic waters that were training to attack undersea cables with a secret sabotage weapon deployed by submersible craft , Reuters has reported, citing western officials. Reuters said its sources declined to detail how the technology works. The confrontation took place near the remote Svalbard archipelago . British and Norwegian officials took their findings to Moscow to show they were aware of the new technology. CIA director John Ratcliffe’s visit to Moscow in August was partly to warn ‌Russia against escalating sabotage operations in Europe, Reuters said, citing two people familiar with the matter. The US has not publicly explained Ratcliffe’s trip. The Norwegian defence minister, Tore Sandvik, told Reuters: “Through our joint operation, we sent a clear message to Russia that they cannot operate covertly … It is in no one’s interest to escalate tensions in the High ‌North.” Britain’s defence ministry pointed to previous statements about attempted covert activities in and near Norwegian and British waters by Russia’s “deep-sea research directorate”, known by the acronym GUGI, which is under international sanctions. The White House did not respond to a comment request, Reuters said, while the CIA declined to comment. The British man Joshua Cammidge, arrested as an alleged Russian agent, was part of a plot to sabotage a drone factory in England, prosecutors said on Thursday in a London court. Cammidge, 31, is charged with engaging in conduct to materially assist a foreign intelligence service in carrying out activities in violation of the National Security Act. He did not enter a plea and was returned to custody until due in court again on 25 September. Cammidge was in contact with a suspected representative of the GRU Volunteer Corps , a group controlled by Russia’s military intelligence agency, the prosecution told Westminster magistrates court. Cammidge allegedly provided information on four drone manufacturing sites in his home town of Swindon. A Ukrainian missile strike caused damage in the south ⁠of the ​Russian city of Volgograd, officials said on Friday. The Volgograd oil refinery ⁠run by Lukoil , one of ​Russia’s ​biggest by ​processing capacity, is ​located ‌in the ​southern ​part of the city. A ⁠Ukrainian drone attack ⁠caused ⁠a fire at ​a warehouse of Russian e-commerce ⁠company ​Ozon ‌in ‌the city of ‌Saratov, the company said on Friday. Russian airstrikes injured eight and caused a ⁠fire in a ⁠nine-storey apartment ​building in Kyiv on Friday morning , city authorities said. Poland and Ukraine stopped⁠ a threat to one of their border crossings and expect they will ⁠be further targeted, Donald Tusk said on Thursday, as ⁠Russia ​attacks wartime routes between Ukraine and its neighbouring allies. “Last night, thanks to cooperation between ​our services and their Ukrainian ‌counterparts, a direct ‌threat to one of the border crossings was averted,” the Polish prime minister said, adding that he had received “a fairly ⁠precise report directly from the CIA regarding possible events ​in the coming months”. Poland also suspended flights at its Lublin and ⁠Rzeszów ​airports on Thursday while its air ‌force conducted ​what were described as preventive operations related to ⁠Russian missile ​attacks on ​Ukraine. On Wednesday, drones hit a border crossing between Ukraine and Moldova in the southern region of ⁠Odesa, killing two people . “We expect similar actions targeting border crossings with Ukraine in other countries, including Poland,” Tusk said. Russia did ‌not immediately comment. A Russian strike on a shopping centre in Pavlohrad, central Ukraine, killed at least five people , authorities said on Thursday . Another 76 people were injured including children, and other parts of the city were also attacked. The city lies on a supply route for the Ukrainian ⁠military connecting central Ukraine to eastern frontlines. Two people were killed by a Russian attack in Dnipro on the ‌US-owned Bunge sunflower oil factory , one of Ukraine’s five largest food plants with a processing capacity of 1,600 tonnes of oilseeds per day. Another five people were injured. “This is no coincidence, but ​part of Moscow’s systematic terror campaign against American businesses and economic interests,” said the Ukrainian foreign minister, Andrii Sybiha. Before Russia started the war, Ukraine was the world’s largest exporter of sunflower ‌oil. Russia has carried out attacks on oilseed refineries and vegetable oil terminals while claiming to be targeting military ports and shipping. Ukraine’s president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, said Russian forces struck the eastern Donetsk region and the Kharkiv ⁠region in the north-east. In the north-eastern city of Sumy, officials ​said a jet-powered drone tore into a shopping centre – a ​day after two people were killed and 20 wounded in a similar attack there. Russian officials said Ukrainian drone attacks ​on the border region of Belgorod killed ‌two people and injured ​seven. Two Azerbaijani tugboat ⁠crew members ⁠were killed ​and two others ⁠injured in a Russian ​attack ‌on ‌civilian shipping ‌in Ukraine’s southern Odesa region, Kyiv’s infrastructure ministry ‌said. Canada offers air defense support for Ukraine as Zelenskyy visits Read more Canada offered support on Thursday to boost Ukraine’s air defences and help replenish its drone stocks , as the countries pledged to deepen their alliance during a visit by Zelenskyy. The support includes C$350m (US$253m) provided through a programme known as Jumpstart run in conjunction with the US. Carney said Ottawa was also offering C$450m in loan guarantees to enhance the Ukrainian energy supply; meanwhile Canada was racing to increase its drone arsenal, from which 30% of Canadian production would go to Ukraine. Russia is illegally trafficking foreigners to fight in Ukraine who quickly become “cannon fodder” , Amnesty International said on Thursday, citing interviews with prisoners of war deceived into signing Russian military contracts. Among the victims were citizens of Brazil, Colombia, Sri Lanka and South Africa lured to Russia through fake job advertisements. “Then it’s coercion. Their passports are taken away. They are made to sign documents they don’t understand,” said Agnes Callamard, Amnesty’s secretary general. “They are given training they don’t understand [and used as] cannon fodder.” Explore more on these topics Ukraine Russia-Ukraine war at a glance Russia Europe Nato explainers Share Reuse this content Most viewed Most viewed World Europe US news Americas Asia Australia Middle East Africa Inequality Global development

https://www.internazionale.it/ultime-not.text: Germany says Russia responsible for drone attack at Leipzig airport La Germania ritiene la Russia responsabile dell’attacco con un drone all’aeroporto di Lipsia Reuters 1.9.2026 A police officer in protective clothing walks next to an explosive-disarming robot (EOD) at Leipzig/Halle Airport in Schkeuditz, Germany, August 5, 2026, after the police said explosives experts examined a drone found near a runway, and after a DHL cargo a ( Reuters ) FOTO D’ARCHIVIO: Un agente di polizia in tenuta protettiva cammina accanto a un robot per il disinnesco di ordigni esplosivi (EOD) all’aeroporto di Lipsia/Halle a Schkeuditz, in Germania, il 5 agosto 2026, dopo che la polizia ha riferito che gli artificieri hanno esaminato un drone rinvenuto nei pressi di una pista e dopo che un aereo cargo della DHL ha urtato un oggetto non identificato mentre decollava dall’aeroporto durante la notte, costringendolo ad un atterraggio non previsto ad Hannover, secondo una fonte a conoscenza dell’incidente. Per saperne di più By Maria Martinez BERLIN, Sept 1 (Reuters) - The German government said on Tuesday that it had concluded that Russia was responsible for an attempted drone attack at Leipzig/Halle Airport last month and ordered a series of measures in response, including the closure of a consulate and a Russian cultural centre in Berlin. Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt said intelligence findings indicated that individuals involved in the attack were acting on behalf of Russian state agencies. “Taken together, police investigations, patterns of the offences and intelligence findings establish Russian responsibility for the attempted attack at Leipzig Airport,” he said. The announcement came at a sensitive political moment in Germany, with the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD), which has called for closer ties with Moscow, leading polls ahead of a state election. The eastern German state of Saxony-Anhalt holds an election on September 6. The AfD currently holds a strong lead in opinion polls, 40% compared with 23% for Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s conservative Christian Democrats. AfD leader Tino Chrupalla in a Welt TV interview accused the German government of “double standards” in blaming Moscow. “Above all, I would have welcomed it if the same had been done in response to Ukraine’s attack on Nord Stream,” Chrupalla said on Tuesday. Germany has been hit by a series of incidents that have prompted authorities to consider how to better protect critical infrastructure against what officials describe as a growing threat from cyber and hybrid attacks. The power grid in the eastern German state of Brandenburg was the target of sabotage on Tuesday after unexploded incendiary devices damaged power lines, the state’s interior minister said, without ruling out the possibility that foreign powers were behind the attack. Standing alongside Dobrindt, Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul said Germany did not view Leipzig as an isolated incident. “It fits into a broader pattern of Russian hybrid operations in Europe,” he said. ‘GERMANY WILL DEFEND ITSELF’ Wadephul said Germany’s response would include closing Russia’s consulate general in Bonn and terminating its agreement with the Russian House cultural centre in Berlin. “Germany remains secure, and Germany will defend itself against adversaries who seek to create insecurity,” Wadephul said. “We will not allow Russia’s attacks to divide or intimidate us in our social cohesion.” Russia’s ambassador to Germany was summoned on Tuesday and he was seen by a Reuters photographer entering the German foreign ministry in Berlin. Responding to Germany’s announcement, Russian Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova said Moscow would respond to what she called Berlin’s “anti-Russian action,” according to Interfax news agency. She did not elaborate. The Russian Embassy in Berlin had previously dismissed such accusations as “fabricated provocation” and as “a new wave of anti-Russian hysteria in Germany.” “If such serious accusations are being made, they should be supported by evidence. To my knowledge, none has been presented,” Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said, according to Russia’s state-run RIA news agency, speaking to reporters in Kyrgyzstan. “It is clear that Germany is pursuing a path of further escalation,” Peskov added. EU COUNTRIES EXPRESS SOLIDARITY WITH GERMANY Germany and Europe more widely face a serious threat from such “hybrid” actions, the interior minister said. “These actions target critical infrastructure, defence companies and support for Ukraine.” Germany will also push within the European Union for additional sanctions listings and travel restrictions on Russian nationals, while increasing pressure on Russia’s “shadow fleet,” Wadephul said. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said she would discuss the attack on Wednesday with NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte, and EU foreign ministers would prepare a joint response. Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk, Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni, UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham and Swedish Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson, among others, expressed support for Germany. “Looking forward to discussing collective countermeasures at the Gymnich meeting in Ireland tonight and tomorrow,” Polish Foreign Minister Radoslaw Sikorski said on X. “Full solidarity with Germany.” “Whenever Russian hybrid activities target one of our allies, we are all exposed,” the Czech Foreign Ministry said on X. Russia’s hybrid activities targeting European states have increased in recent years. Poland, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania and Romania have all confirmed various forms of violations and hostile actions, Sweden’s Kristersson said. Prime Minister Andy Burnham said that any Russian attempts to undermine support for Ukraine were “doomed to fail.” Wadephul said Germany would “continue its civilian and military support for Ukraine and will resolutely continue its solidarity with Ukraine in its defence against Russia’s war of aggression.” (Reporting by Maria Martinez and James Mackenzie, additional reporting by Alan Charlish, William James, Ronald Popeski, Jan Lopatka, Simon Johnson, Miranda Murray, Fabrizio Bensch and Kirsti Knolle.Editing by Gareth Jones, Kevin Liffey and Sanjeev Miglani) Di Maria Martinez BERLINO, 1 settembre (Reuters) - Martedì il governo tedesco ha dichiarato di aver concluso che la Russia è responsabile di un tentato attacco con droni all’aeroporto di Lipsia/Halle avvenuto il mese scorso e ha ordinato una serie di misure in risposta, tra cui la chiusura di un consolato e di un centro culturale russo a Berlino. Il ministro dell’Interno Alexander Dobrindt ha affermato che i risultati delle indagini dei servizi segreti indicano che le persone coinvolte nell’attacco agivano per conto di agenzie statali russe. «Nel loro insieme, le indagini della polizia, le modalità dei reati e i risultati delle indagini dei servizi segreti stabiliscono la responsabilità russa per il tentato attacco all’aeroporto di Lipsia», ha dichiarato. L’annuncio è giunto in un momento politico delicato in Germania, con il partito di estrema destra Alternativa per la Germania (AfD), che ha invocato legami più stretti con Mosca, in testa ai sondaggi in vista di un’elezione regionale. Lo Stato della Sassonia-Anhalt, nella Germania orientale, terrà le elezioni il 6 settembre. L’AfD detiene attualmente un forte vantaggio nei sondaggi, con il 40% rispetto al 23% dei cristiano-democratici conservatori del cancelliere Friedrich Merz. Il leader dell’AfD Tino Chrupalla, in un’intervista alla Welt TV, ha accusato il governo tedesco di «due pesi e due misure» nel dare la colpa a Mosca. «Soprattutto, avrei gradito che si fosse agito allo stesso modo in risposta all’attacco dell’Ucraina al Nord Stream», ha affermato Chrupalla martedì. La Germania è stata colpita da una serie di incidenti che hanno spinto le autorità a valutare come proteggere meglio le infrastrutture critiche da quella che i funzionari descrivono come una crescente minaccia derivante da attacchi informatici e ibridi. Martedì la rete elettrica dello stato tedesco orientale del Brandeburgo è stata oggetto di un atto di sabotaggio dopo che ordigni incendiari inesplosi hanno danneggiato le linee elettriche, ha affermato il ministro dell’Interno dello stato, senza escludere la possibilità che dietro l’attacco ci fossero potenze straniere. Al fianco di Dobrindt, il ministro degli esteri Johann Wadephul ha affermato che la Germania non considera quanto accaduto a Lipsia un episodio isolato. «Si inserisce in un quadro più ampio di operazioni ibride russe in Europa», ha dichiarato. «LA GERMANIA SI DIFENDERÀ» Wadephul ha dichiarato che la risposta della Germania comprenderà la chiusura del consolato generale russo a Bonn e la rescissione dell’accordo con il centro culturale «Russian House» di Berlino. «La Germania rimane al sicuro e si difenderà dagli avversari che cercano di creare insicurezza», ha dichiarato Wadephul. «Non permetteremo che gli attacchi della Russia ci dividano o ci intimidiscano nella nostra coesione sociale». Martedì l’ambasciatore russo in Germania è stato convocato ed è stato visto da un fotografo di Reuters mentre entrava nel ministero degli Esteri tedesco a Berlino. In risposta all’annuncio della Germania, la portavoce del ministero degli Esteri russo Maria Zakharova ha affermato che Mosca avrebbe reagito a quella che ha definito «azione anti-russa» di Berlino, secondo quanto riportato dall’agenzia di stampa Interfax. Non ha fornito ulteriori dettagli. L’Ambasciata russa a Berlino aveva precedentemente respinto tali accuse definendole «provocazioni inventate» e «una nuova ondata di isteria anti-russa in Germania». «Se vengono mosse accuse così gravi, dovrebbero essere supportate da prove. Per quanto ne so, non ne è stata presentata alcuna», ha dichiarato il portavoce del Cremlino Dmitry Peskov, secondo l’agenzia di stampa statale russa RIA, parlando ai giornalisti in Kirghizistan. «È chiaro che la Germania sta perseguendo una strada di ulteriore escalation», ha aggiunto Peskov. I PAESI DELL’UNIONE EUROPEA ESPRIMONO SOLIDARIETÀ CON LA GERMANIA La Germania e l’Europa in generale devono affrontare una grave minaccia derivante da tali azioni “ibride”, ha affermato il ministro dell’Interno. “Queste azioni prendono di mira le infrastrutture critiche, le aziende del settore della difesa e il sostegno all’Ucraina”. La Germania spingerà inoltre, all’interno dell’Unione europea, per l’inserimento di ulteriori nomi nelle liste delle sanzioni e per l’imposizione di restrizioni di viaggio ai cittadini russi, aumentando al contempo la pressione sulla “flotta ombra” russa, ha affermato Wadephul. La presidente della Commissione europea Ursula von der Leyen ha dichiarato che mercoledì discuterà dell’attacco con il segretario generale della NATO Mark Rutte, e che i ministri degli esteri dell’Unione europea prepareranno una risposta congiunta. Il primo ministro polacco Donald Tusk, la prima ministra italiana Giorgia Meloni, il primo ministro britannico Andy Burnham e il primo ministro svedese Ulf Kristersson, tra gli altri, hanno espresso il loro sostegno alla Germania. «Non vedo l’ora di discutere delle contromisure collettive durante la riunione di Gymnich in Irlanda stasera e domani», ha dichiarato su X il ministro degli esteri polacco Radoslaw Sikorski. «Piena solidarietà con la Germania». «Ogni volta che le attività ibride russe prendono di mira uno dei nostri alleati, siamo tutti esposti», ha affermato il Ministero degli Esteri ceco su X. Le attività ibride della Russia rivolte contro gli Stati europei sono aumentate negli ultimi anni. Polonia, Estonia, Lettonia, Lituania e Romania hanno tutte confermato varie forme di violazioni e azioni ostili, ha affermato il primo ministro svedese Kristersson. Il primo ministro Andy Burnham ha affermato che qualsiasi tentativo russo di minare il sostegno all’Ucraina è «destinato a fallire». Wadephul ha affermato che la Germania «continuerà a fornire sostegno civile e militare all’Ucraina e proseguirà con determinazione la propria solidarietà con l’Ucraina nella sua difesa contro la guerra di aggressione della Russia». (Reporter Maria Martinez e James Mackenzie, con contributi aggiuntivi di Alan Charlish, William James, Ronald Popeski, Jan Lopatka, Simon Johnson, Miranda Murray, Fabrizio Bensch e Kirsti Knolle. https://telex.hu/belfold/2026/10/16/maso.text: Menü Kereső 1944-ben lelőtt szovjet vadászgép roncsait ásták ki öt méter mélyről Belföld Bakró-Nagy Ferenc Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom Második világháborús Jak–1B-s szovjet vadászgép roncsai kerültek elő 520 centiméter mélyről Törtelnél a közelmúltban, a leleteket később kiállításon mutatják be – közölte Magó Károly, a 86. Szolnok Helikopterdandár zászlósa, roncskutató pénteken a Szolnokon tartott sajtótájékoztatón. Ismertetése szerint a roncsra a HM Hadtörténeti Intézet és Múzeum, illetve a helikopterdandár munkatársai és a Magyar Roncskutató Egyesület tagjai együttműködésének eredményeként találtak rá. A történeti háttérről elmondta, hogy 1944. november elején Törtel határában a német Peter Düttmann hadnagy és a szovjet Alexandr Szemjonovics Andrianov gárda-hadnagy légi harcot vívott, a szovjet gépet a német pilóta lelőtte. Andrianov sikeresen kiugrott a repülőgépből és fogságba esett. A roncs felkutatását Kocsis István, a Magyar Roncskutató Egyesület egyik alapító tagja kezdte el, szemtanúkat hallgatott meg és sikerült a helyszínt leszűkítenie. A feltárás során megállapították, hogy a repülőgép nagy sebességgel csapódott a földbe, a vegyes építésű gép apró darabokra szakadt szét – számolt be Magó Károly. Sikerült kiemelni a repülőgép fő darabjait a futóműből és a motorból is, továbbá a repülőgép vászonborításából is jelentősebb felület maradt meg. Rajta van a vörös csillag egy darabja viszonylag jó állapotban és a vászonszerkezetből olyan darab is előkerült, amelyen a repülőgép oldalszáma látható. Ezen felül a pilóta néhány személyes tárgya is előkerült. Fotó: Mészáros János / MTVA Maga a típus is kuriózum, ilyen jelentős lelet még nem került elő Jak–1-es gépből. A repülőgépet azért lehetett azonosítani, mert az úgynevezett sárkányszerkezet és a motor száma is előkerült különböző alkatrészeken, így egyértelmű, hogy a gárda-hadnagy vezette repülőgép került elő – közölte Magó Károly. Érdekességként megemlítette, hogy találtak egy könyvet is, amelyen a pilóta aláírása is kivehető, azt jelenleg restaurálják a HM Hadtörténeti Intézet és Múzeumban. A régi szolnoki repülőmúzeumban tartott sajtótájékoztatón bemutattak később kiállítható, illetve nem beazonosítható, nagyon összeroncsolódott leleteket, utóbbiakat raktározzák majd. A kiállításon látható tárgyak örökségvédelem alá kerülnek, Szolnokon tárolják majd azokat, a látványosabb, jobb állapotban lévő darabokat a HM Hadtörténeti Intézet és Múzeum fogja kiállítani – tájékoztatott Magó Károly. Kocsis István az MTI-nek elmondta, hogy már szeptemberben elkezdődtek az előkutatások. A feltárás régészeti és „baleset-kivizsgálási módszertannal” zajlott, utána a laza talajszerkezet miatt a mélyebben lévő részeket már tömbös módszerrel emelték ki, azaz a markoló nagy földdarabokat emelt ki és azokat tisztították meg a gödör mellett. Polgár Balázs régész-muzeológus, a HM Hadtörténeti Intézet és Múzeum hadirégészeti részlegének vezetője arról beszélt, hogy a tárgyi emlékeket állagmegóvás során tisztítják, konzerválják, majd a gyűjteményi alapleltárba kerülnek. Tudományosan feldolgozzák azokat és hamarosan publikációban, kiállításon is bemutathatják az eredményeket, tárgyi emlékeket. Kedvenceink Partnereinktől Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! https://campaignbrief.com/gerri-hamills-.text: TVC Directory Advertise Jobs Rankings Agencies Creative Directors Executive CDs Creatives Clients TVC Directors TVC Companies BestAdsOnTV.com Portfolio & Reel Filters Agencies Campaigns Awards Expat News News New Business Opinion People Moves Seen+Noted TVC Production Archive ASIA AUS NZ WA Gerri Hamill’s LIA Diary #2: Final debates, tough calls and a defining career moment October 5 2026, 11:27 am | BY Ricki Green | No Comments Gerri Hamill, Head of Production, WPP@Unilever / Director of Integrated Production, VML Singapore, is representing Singapore on the Health & Wellness and Pharma Craft jury at LIA in Vegas. Here, Gerri, along with a number of other jurors from APAC, reports exclusively for CB. Day 3… wrap day and awards!! Well, the big day has come and gone. Final debates. Final collaborations and conversations have been reviewed and settled. There’s been so much excitement, with so much wealth of talent, it’s been a tough call. For me, it was the freshness, originality and innovation I was looking for in the work. To exchange preferences and voice my opinions to the whole panel brought a sense of pleasure to me. At the end of the day, with so much good work to be recognised, tough decisions had to be made. After all, we were judging the work of the future rising stars of industry from forty countries around the world. Well, we did it. Statues are ready to be awarded and it’s all over until next year. To be a member of the 2026 LIA jury will remain a defining moment in my career. I was also talking with fellow VML colleague Julia Dovlatova, ECD, VML Czechia, who said of her jury: “We wrapped Digital and Creators & Social Platforms with zero fights or grumps or disagreements, despite having had very different opinions on a couple of pieces, and I consider it a great success!
